findings.reason: A one-dimensional spacetime picture materially clarifies three distinct sets already defined: the closed backward triangle, lateral sides with excluded vertex but included base rim, and the open base ball. The original text renders correctly; this is a warranted explanatory addition under expanded diagram scope, not a claim that diagrams are required for validity.
findings.action: Added final Remarks with a native TikZ characteristic triangle, forward bounding rays and separate open-base interval.

correction: Added an explanatory n=1, t_0>0 spacetime illustration without changing the original Definition or any metadata. The caption distinguishes closure of the full cone from the open base ball and the excluded lateral-boundary vertex.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Points (x,t) in R x R, fixed c>0, x_0 in R and t_0>0. Figure coordinates use independent spatial and time scales: x=x_0+(ct_0/2.4)X and t=(t_0/2.4)Y.
diagram_math_checks.relations: Triangle vertices (-2.4,0), (2.4,0), (0,2.4) represent (x_0-ct_0,0), (x_0+ct_0,0), (x_0,t_0). Edges satisfy x=x_0±c(t_0-t); the shaded interior satisfies |x-x_0|≤c(t_0-t), 0≤t≤t_0.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Direct substitution into Definition lines 37–46 and the explicit one-dimensional characteristic description at lines 71–73. The triangle has three vertices and three explicitly drawn closing edges; each vertex has degree two in the backward boundary.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Backward cone vertex, base endpoints, and lateral boundary.
diagram_math_checks.relations: All three marked vertices belong to closed K^-. Lateral boundary consists of the two sloping sides with vertex removed and base endpoints retained. The caption explicitly excludes the vertex from the lateral boundary even though the vertex belongs to the cone.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 48–49 require 0≤t<t_0 and equality |x-x_0|=c(t_0-t); t=0 yields the two included endpoints, while t=t_0 is excluded.

diagram_math_checks.relations: In figure coordinates Y≥2.4 and X=±(Y-2.4), hence x=x_0±c(t-t_0). Arrows point toward larger time and no artificial top edge closes the unbounded region.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 50–52 gives t≥t_0 and |x-x_0|≤c(t-t_0). The caption calls these bounding rays and explicitly states indefinite continuation.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Separate open base interval drawn below the axis.
diagram_math_checks.relations: Its endpoints denote x_0±ct_0 but are excluded, so it represents (x_0-ct_0,x_0+ct_0)×{0}; the displacement to Y=-0.85 is explicitly only presentational.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Definition lines 39–41 defines B_r using strict inequality; lines 48 and 73 identify the open base ball and interval. Hollow rings implement strict endpoints, distinct from the cone’s closed base rim.

diagram_math_checks.relations: The illustration asserts no new propagation or uniqueness theorem and supplies no premise for an argument.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original text through line 77 remains byte-identical. The definition already states the geometric formulas and directs propagation/uniqueness to separate results. Mathematical definitions and rigorous arguments remain independent of the figure.

evidence.visual_checks: Native SSR TikZ compiled to SVG without error. Standalone original-resolution tile 02 shows all three backward boundary edges, white closed vertex/base points, two continuing forward rays, readable labels and blue shaded interior with adequate white-stroke contrast. Both open endpoint circles have black centres and white outlines. SVG confirms open-ring fill=var(--background, transparent), while closed points have foreground fill. No overlap or clipping in complete figure.

checks.result: Completed native local manifest and two PNG captures; inspected both at original resolution.

limitations: Illustration specializes to n=1 and t_0>0, stated explicitly; higher-dimensional and degenerate cases retain the original exact definition.
